verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.54
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 7.54

verses.pali: 6. Abyākatavagga
verses.english: 6. The Undeclared Points

verses.pali: Abyākatasutta
verses.english: The Undeclared Points

verses.pali: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

verses.pali: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo yena sutavato ariyasāvakassa vicikicchā nuppajjati abyākatavatthūsū”ti?
verses.english: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why a learned noble disciple has no doubts regarding the undeclared points?”

verses.pali: “Diṭṭhinirodhā kho, bhikkhu, sutavato ariyasāvakassa vicikicchā nuppajjati abyākatavatthūsu.
verses.english: “Mendicant, it’s due to the cessation of views that a learned noble disciple has no doubts regarding the undeclared points.

verses.pali: ‘Hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti kho, bhikkhu, diṭṭhigatametaṁ;
verses.english: ‘A realized one still exists after death’: this is a misconception.

verses.pali: ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti kho, bhikkhu, diṭṭhigatametaṁ;
verses.english: ‘A realized one no longer exists after death’: this is a misconception.

verses.pali: ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti kho, bhikkhu, diṭṭhigatametaṁ;
verses.english: ‘A realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death’: this is a misconception.

verses.pali: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti kho, bhikkhu, diṭṭhigatametaṁ.
verses.english: ‘A realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death’: this is a misconception.

verses.pali: Assutavā, bhikkhu, puthujjano diṭṭhiṁ nappajānāti, diṭṭhisamudayaṁ nappajānāti, diṭṭhinirodhaṁ nappajānāti, diṭṭhinirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ nappajānāti.
verses.english: An unlearned ordinary person doesn’t understand views, their origin, their cessation, or the practice that leads to their cessation.

verses.pali: Tassa sā diṭṭhi pavaḍḍhati, so na parimuccati jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi. ‘Na parimuccati dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: And so their views grow. They’re not freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They’re not freed from suffering, I say.

verses.pali: Sutavā ca kho, bhikkhu, ariyasāvako diṭṭhiṁ pajānāti, diṭṭhisamudayaṁ pajānāti, diṭṭhinirodhaṁ pajānāti, diṭṭhinirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānāti.
verses.english: A learned noble disciple does understand views, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

verses.pali: Tassa sā diṭṭhi nirujjhati, so parimuccati jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi. ‘Parimuccati dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: And so their views cease. They’re freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They’re freed from suffering, I say.

verses.pali: Evaṁ jānaṁ kho, bhikkhu, sutavā ariyasāvako evaṁ passaṁ ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na byākaroti;
verses.english: Knowing and seeing this, a learned noble disciple does not answer: ‘A realized one still exists after death’,

verses.pali: ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na byākaroti;
verses.english: ‘A realized one no longer exists after death’,

verses.pali: ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na byākaroti;
verses.english: ‘a realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death’,

verses.pali: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na byākaroti.
verses.english: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

verses.pali: Evaṁ jānaṁ kho, bhikkhu, sutavā ariyasāvako evaṁ passaṁ evaṁ abyākaraṇadhammo hoti abyākatavatthūsu.
verses.english: Knowing and seeing this, a learned noble disciple does not declare the undeclared points.

verses.pali: Evaṁ jānaṁ kho, bhikkhu, sutavā ariyasāvako evaṁ passaṁ na chambhati, na kampati, na vedhati, na santāsaṁ āpajjati abyākatavatthūsu.
verses.english: Knowing and seeing this, a learned noble disciple doesn’t shake, tremble, quake, or get nervous regarding the undeclared points.

verses.pali: ‘Hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti kho, bhikkhu, taṇhāgatametaṁ …pe…
verses.english: ‘A realized one still exists after death’: this is just about craving. …

verses.pali: saññāgatametaṁ …pe…
verses.english: it’s just about perception …

verses.pali: maññitametaṁ …pe…
verses.english: it’s a conceiving …

verses.pali: papañcitametaṁ …pe…
verses.english: it’s a proliferation …

verses.pali: upādānagatametaṁ …pe…
verses.english: it’s just about grasping …

verses.pali: ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti kho, bhikkhu, vippaṭisāro eso;
verses.english: ‘A realized one still exists after death’: this is a regret.

verses.pali: ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti kho, bhikkhu, vippaṭisāro eso;
verses.english: ‘A realized one no longer exists after death’: this is a regret.

verses.pali: ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti kho, bhikkhu, vippaṭisāro eso;
verses.english: ‘A realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death’: this is a regret.

verses.pali: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti kho, bhikkhu, vippaṭisāro eso.
verses.english: ‘A realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death’: this is a regret.

verses.pali: Assutavā, bhikkhu, puthujjano vippaṭisāraṁ nappajānāti, vippaṭisārasamudayaṁ nappajānāti, vippaṭisāranirodhaṁ nappajānāti, vippaṭisāranirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ nappajānāti.
verses.english: An unlearned ordinary person doesn’t understand regrets, their origin, their cessation, or the practice that leads to their cessation.

verses.pali: Tassa so vippaṭisāro pavaḍḍhati, so na parimuccati jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi. ‘Na parimuccati dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: And so their regrets grow. They’re not freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They’re not freed from suffering, I say.

verses.pali: Sutavā ca kho, bhikkhu, ariyasāvako vippaṭisāraṁ pajānāti, vippaṭisārasamudayaṁ pajānāti, vippaṭisāranirodhaṁ pajānāti, vippaṭisāranirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānāti.
verses.english: A learned noble disciple does understand regrets, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

verses.pali: Tassa so vippaṭisāro nirujjhati, so parimuccati jātiyā …pe… ‘… dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: And so their regrets cease. They’re freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They’re freed from suffering, I say.

verses.pali: Evaṁ jānaṁ kho, bhikkhu, sutavā ariyasāvako evaṁ passaṁ ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na byākaroti …pe…
verses.english: Knowing and seeing this, a learned noble disciple does not answer: ‘A realized one still exists after death’ …

verses.pali: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’tipi na byākaroti.
verses.english: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

verses.pali: Evaṁ jānaṁ kho, bhikkhu, sutavā ariyasāvako evaṁ passaṁ evaṁ abyākaraṇadhammo hoti abyākatavatthūsu.
verses.english: Knowing and seeing this, a learned noble disciple does not declare the undeclared points.

verses.pali: Evaṁ jānaṁ kho, bhikkhu, sutavā ariyasāvako evaṁ passaṁ na chambhati, na kampati, na vedhati, na santāsaṁ āpajjati abyākatavatthūsu.
verses.english: Knowing and seeing this, a learned noble disciple doesn’t shake, tremble, quake, or get nervous regarding the undeclared points.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhu, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yena sutavato ariyasāvakassa vicikicchā nuppajjati abyākatavatthūsū”ti.
verses.english: This is the cause, this is the reason why a learned noble disciple has no doubts regarding the undeclared points.”

verses.pali: Paṭhamaṁ.
